## Windows compatibility review — `038735dfeb`

Reviewed at head `038735dfeba25e9c5add1b8184a0f5bcde58c2ff` (base `55b335eb87`). Scope: the whole diff (2 files) — a `huggingface` pattern and a `cookie` pattern in `_PATTERNS`, `hf_` added to the truncated-tail prefix list, and the new cases.

**No Windows compatibility issue found.**

Pure text processing: no path, subprocess, encoding, or platform branch; the patterns run over the same strings on every platform.

On reading the patterns:

- `hf_` keeps the house lookbehind (`(?<![A-Za-z0-9_])`) so a token inside a longer identifier is not half-matched, and the 20-char floor plus the added `hf_` tail prefix cover both a full token and one a call-record cap truncated.
- The `cookie` pattern redacts only the value after `Cookie:` / `Set-Cookie:` (header name and colon survive, so `curl -H 'Cookie: [redacted]'` stays readable). A quoted value stops at the quote, a header line stops at CR/LF, and the `{6,}` floor keeps short non-secrets such as `cookie: none` untouched — both directions are pinned by the negative cases added here.

Verification, native Windows host (GitHub tarball of `038735dfeb`, extracted under `D:\tmp\rv1361`):

- `python -S runner.py tests/test_acp_redact.py -q` → `55 passed`

Gaps: the redaction is verified through the unit suite only (no live tool-output capture); the tree is the commit's export rather than a git worktree.

<!-- raven-windows-review:pr=1361;head=038735dfeba25e9c5add1b8184a0f5bcde58c2ff;reviewer=LivXue -->

## Windows compatibility review

Scope: full base-to-head diff at `ccb5218b4f68f9c2c04b5700f426166c4264e53c` (base now `fc0a30f768`; head is a merge of `origin/main` into the branch). The effective PR diff is 2 files: `raven/security/redact.py` (+4/-1) and `tests/test_acp_redact.py` (+5). After the merge the PR's own change is the HF token pattern `(?<![A-Za-z0-9_])(hf_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,})`, the Cookie/Set-Cookie value pattern, and `hf_` added to the truncated-tail patterns.

Result: **no Windows compatibility issue.** Both patterns are pure text regexes with no path, subprocess, or filesystem surface. The Cookie pattern explicitly excludes `\r\n` from the value class, so a CRLF header on Windows is cut at the line end rather than swallowing the next line; verified by the tests and by reading the class.

Checks on this native Windows host, from the head tree (tarball checkout):

```
python -S runner.py tests/test_acp_redact.py -q
-> 62 passed   (57 at the base tree: the 5 new cases pass)
```

`tests/test_trajectory_redact.py` in the same run: 3 failed, 87 passed; the identical three IDs fail at the base tree (3 failed, 82 passed):
`test_residual_finding_carries_token_and_occurrences`, `test_binary_file_excluded_and_recorded`, `test_end_to_end_report_with_real_tracer`. All three compare `artifacts\tool.output.json` against `artifacts/tool.output.json` (and one keys a report by an OS-separator path) — inherited Windows separator assumptions in the trajectory scanner's tests, not this PR's patterns.

Gaps: tarball checkout; the merge was not re-verified against every mainline file beyond the effective diff.

<!-- raven-windows-review:pr=1361;head=ccb5218b4f68f9c2c04b5700f426166c4264e53c;reviewer=LivXue -->

Closing this in favour of a smaller surface.

We have settled on keeping the redaction table at the scale Codex uses: four well-known patterns, rather than one rule per vendor. Under that direction a Hugging Face prefix rule and a Cookie header rule are outside what this module is meant to enumerate, however correct the underlying observations were.

Two notes for the record. The `hf_` half was sound: the left boundary avoids the false positives the rest of the table pays for on short opaque words, and the review found no rewritten ordinary text. It simply is not a rule class we are keeping. The Cookie half had a real problem in both directions: it rewrote ordinary source such as `cookie: Optional[str] = None` (an in-repo instance is `raven/rpc/serve_control.py`), while quoted values like `Cookie: "session=abc"` and the structured `{"Cookie": "..."}` shape on rawInput were not redacted at all.

Thanks for the careful write-up; the `read_file` and `rawInput` reasoning in the description is what made the comparison decidable.
